page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware allocation includes 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. System memory totals 24.0 GB, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it is provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a profile suited for moderate workloads. The shared CPU allocation results in a poor stress-ng single-core CPU performance and a weak multi-core CPU performance. Geekbench testing shows an average single-core score but a weak multi-core score, alongside weak results in software compilation and image processing. However, memory bandwidth for small cached blocks and write operations on large blocks remains average. Text processing, bzip3 decompression, and Passmark CPU tests, including encryption and physics, also perform within average ranges.

Given the shared CPU allocation and weak database and static web serving benchmark results, this server is not optimized for high-throughput database operations or heavy web traffic. It offers qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense, memory-leaning workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. Appropriate workloads include lightweight background processing, development environments, text processing, and basic utility services that benefit from 24.0 GB of RAM without demanding continuous multi-core processing power.
